summary.text: A female patient presented at age 15, now 19, to a family medicine clinic with primary amenorrhea and absent secondary sexual characteristics. She had one episode of vaginal spotting 2 years earlier, no hirsutism, galactorrhea, visual disturbance, anosmia or cyclic pelvic pain, normal growth and development, a normal BMI, and a family history of diabetes and an older sister with amenorrhea; her parents were consanguineous.

Laboratory evaluation showed markedly elevated FSH, elevated TSH rising on repeat, and normal prolactin, free T4, free T3 and thyroid antibodies, with a 46,XX karyotype. She was diagnosed with subclinical hypothyroidism and started on levothyroxine. Pelvic MRI showed poorly visualized atrophic ovaries, a rudimentary or absent uterus and duplicated right renal collecting system and ureters, leading to a diagnosis of MRKH syndrome type II with urogenital anomalies; renal ultrasound confirmed the duplication.

One year later she presented with a 2-week history of headache, fatigue, polyuria and polydipsia; home random glucose exceeded 300 mg/dL, fasting glucose was 126 mg/dL, HbA1c 9.76% with normal C-peptide and insulin, negative diabetes autoantibodies and glycosuria without ketones. Diabetes was confirmed at age 16. She and her guardian initially refused drug treatment but later consented to initiate metformin and sitagliptin.

She was referred to endocrinology for genetic evaluation of possible monogenic diabetes such as MODY, which was suspected. At the time of reporting, genetic testing could not be completed because she and her mother did not attend the sampling appointment, and a full gynecological examination was not possible because of patient refusal.

article_limitations: A source conflict is recorded for the uterus (rudimentary uterine bud in the MRI text vs absent in Table 2, the Fig. 2 caption and the abstract); both sides are review_only. The ovary wording (poorly visualized, not visualized, absent) and the diabetes type (type 2 in the discussion vs suspected MODY) are recorded as ambiguities; the Table 2 absent-ovaries cell and the type 2 statement are review_only.
Genetic testing for MODY (HNF1B sequencing) was requested but not completed; the source calls the results pending and then says testing could not be completed. No genetic result exists.
Table 2 Referral for MODY genetic testing carries a placeholder status cell (Pending/Completed/Not available) and is recorded with unknown status.

Discussion and lessons sentences about HNF1B mutations and a possible link to MRKH are speculative or general and are not recorded as patient facts; the multidisciplinary-approach statement is not recorded as a care plan because the source does not document which specialties actually evaluated her.
Metformin and sitagliptin are recorded with action unknown: the source states only consent to initiate; start, dose and response are not stated.
Only table-governed times (ages in Table 2) and explicit time phrases are recorded; most text facts have no governing time.
Caption-layer visual status is not_inspected; the three JPEGs are inspected in the separate visual submission.
No supplements are listed in the source and no follow-up outcome is reported.
